subject: Post-call: payment & onboarding options for pilot (PO vs card)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Carter <jill.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: procurement & payment options for pilot — next steps

Hi Jill,

Thanks again for the time this morning — helpful conversation. Quick written recap so we can align with Acme Health's AP and legal teams and avoid surprises: 

• Procurement readiness: you mentioned vendor onboarding requires (1) completed vendor questionnaire, (2) W-9, and (3) certificate of insurance. Can you confirm whether there is an internal vendor code that gets assigned and how long setup typically takes once we submit a full packet?

• Payment path: from our notes AP prefers purchase orders for recurring or >$5k annual spend. For pilots under $5k, a corporate card or ACH is usually OK. Can you confirm the threshold you’d like us to price against for a 90-day pilot?

• Marketplace vs direct vendor: you asked whether Redwood is on the CloudHealth marketplace — we are listed, and onboarding via marketplace can shave vendor setup time. If procurement prefers that route we can share the listing ID and seller paperwork.

Attachments I’m including to speed things up: short vendor questionnaire (blank), our standard SLA/terms summary. If you want, I can schedule a 20-minute vendor-portal walkthrough with your onboarding team.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm preferred payment path (PO vs card) for the pilot and AP contact to own vendor setup
2) We send a 90-day SOW + pricing that fits the preferred payment path (we can scope a $3.8k pilot to sit under $5k if card/ACH is required)
3) If PO is required for production scale, we’ll prioritize completed paperwork to vendor onboarding mailbox

Looking forward to your confirmation — thanks!

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0143

Attachments:
- vendor-questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
- redwood-sla-terms-1.2.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Jill Carter <jill.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: procurement & payment options for pilot — next steps

Vanessa,

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick clarifications: 

• Onboarding SLA: standard is 30 business days after we receive complete docs. If vendor is already in CloudHealth marketplace we can expedite to ~10 business days.
• PO threshold: AP prefers POs for recurring services or any contract > $5,000 annually. For pilots/subscriptions under $5k we accept card or ACH.
• Required files: send the completed questionnaire, W-9, and COI to procurement@acmehealth.com. Legal will need to review the SLA/terms (expect 3–5 business days for redlines).

I’ve looped in procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) to own vendor setup and PO issuance. If you can get paperwork to them this week we should be able to have a PO within ~2 weeks.

Best,
Jill Carter
Head of Digital Transformation, Acme Health
jill.carter@acmehealth.com

Hi Procurement team — thanks for the details and quick turnaround. A few items to keep timelines tight: 

• I’ve attached a completed vendor-questionnaire and our W-9 to this thread. Please confirm when you have a vendor record created and any outstanding fields we need to complete.
• Pricing: to make the pilot flow under $5k we can propose a 90-day pilot SOW at $3,800 (license + 250k tokens/day cap). If you’d rather issue a PO we can convert the pilot to a PO-backed SOW and keep the same scope.
• Contracting: our standard approach is MSA + SOW. If legal needs to redline SLA sections, we request a 48-hour turnaround for redlines so onboarding doesn’t slip.

If marketplace onboarding is easier on your side, please share the marketplace seller id and we’ll coordinate with the marketplace team.
